{{Short description|Mathematical theory}}
In [[stable homotopy theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], the '''sphere spectrum''' ''S'' is the monoidal unit in the category of [[spectrum (homotopy theory)|spectra]]. It is the [[suspension spectrum]] of ''S''<sup>0</sup>, i.e., a set of two points. Explicitly, the ''n''-th space in the sphere spectrum is the ''n''-dimensional [[sphere (geometry)|sphere]] ''S''<sup>''n''</sup>, and the structure maps from the [[suspension (mathematics)|suspension]] of ''S''<sup>''n''</sup> to ''S''<sup>''n''+1</sup> are the canonical [[homeomorphism]]s. The ''k''-th homotopy group of a sphere spectrum is the ''k''-th [[stable homotopy group]] of spheres.

The [[Localization of a topological space|localization]] of the sphere spectrum at a prime number ''p'' is called the '''local sphere''' at ''p'' and is denoted by <math>S_{(p)}</math>.
